title: Rebuild a struct from its accesses
description:
A reverse engineer has collected every memory access a function makes through one struct pointer: each one an offset and a size in bytes (1, 2, 4 or 8). Write `guessLayout(accesses)`, which turns them into a list of fields, the way a disassembler's "create structure" feature does:

- Each distinct offset becomes one field. If an offset was accessed with different sizes, use the largest.
- Fields are listed in order of offset.
- Each field's type name comes from its size: 1 `"uint8_t"`, 2 `"uint16_t"`, 4 `"uint32_t"`, 8 `"uint64_t"`.
- Gaps between fields (bytes not covered by any field) become padding fields named `"pad"` of type `"uint8_t[N]"`, where N is the gap size, so the offsets add up. There is no padding after the last field.

```
accesses: {0x0,4} {0x10,8} {0xC,4} {0x0,4}
fields:   0x0 uint32_t
          0x4 uint8_t[8]   (pad)
          0xC uint32_t
          0x10 uint64_t
```
hints: A `std::map<offset, size>` both removes duplicate offsets and keeps them sorted. When the same offset appears again, keep the larger size.
Walk the map keeping `at`, the first byte not yet covered. If the next field starts after `at`, add a padding field of `offset - at` bytes first; after each field, `at = offset + size`.
Real fields need some name that is not `"pad"`: `field_` followed by the offset in hex is the usual convention. `std::format("field_{:X}", offset)` (from `<format>`, as in lesson 1.02) builds it.
lessonTitle: Structs, Arrays and Pointers in Assembly
